rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance - Annual Rent Increase Cap
rules.requirement: Newark's Rent Control Board cannot approve a rent increase of more than 25% in any one year for any tenant, counting all increases (ordinary, major improvement, and hardship increases) together. A landlord may also receive only one rent increase under the ordinary increase section for the same apartment in any twelve-month period.
rules.key_value: Max 25% total increase per year; one ordinary increase per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to housing space in dwellings covered by Newark's rent control chapter (ch. 19:2), unless the unit qualifies for an exemption (e.g., newly constructed, substantially rehabilitated, or certain city-owned dwellings currently within their exemption period).
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed or substandard multiple dwellings and certain city-owned dwellings sold for rehabilitation may be exempt from rent control for a stated exemption period (e.g., 5 years for qualifying city-owned dwelling sales).
rules.quoted_span: Since an immediate rent increase of more than 25% above the prior monthly rent may be considered unconscionable and imposes a hardship on a tenant, the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the building currently qualifies for a rent control exemption (e.g., as newly constructed, substantially rehabilitated, or a qualifying formerly city-owned dwelling within its exemption period)

rules.conflict_note: Exact section number for this 25% annual cap provision is inferred from context (it is referenced alongside and follows sections 19:2-3, 19:2-7, and 19:2-8 in the ordinance) rather than stated directly in the chunk; most recent amendment date shown is 5-20-2026 (Ord. No. 6PSF-B).
